role: Owns the SettingsManager singleton: loads/saves UserSettings JSON (user_settings.json in the App Group container) with a protection-aware don't-clobber guard, off-main coalesced writes, CloudKit export/restore hooks, custom tags, baseline updates, device-local disclaimer flag and trial-clock helpers.
types: SettingsManager.WriteState: struct (private) — pending snapshot + scheduled flag for the write queue
state: mem:SettingsManager.settings (@Observable UserSettings; didSet persists + posts notification)
mem:SettingsManager.settingsSnapshot / snapshotBox (OSAllocatedUnfairLock mirror for off-main readers)
ud:perf.enableAIAssistant / perf.enableVoiceMode / perf.enableWatchConnectivity (standard; mirrors written in save())
toplevel: `nonisolated static let shared = SettingsManager()` creates the singleton lazily on first touch from any thread; settingsWriteQueue and writeState are created as stored-property initializers. Notification.Name.flowRecoverySettingsChanged = "FlowRecoverySettingsChanged".

flags.text: The protection-aware load path (blockedByProtection, retryLoadAfterUnlock, the didSet don't-clobber guard) has no test in EmuquTests (grep for blockedByProtection/retryLoadAfterUnlock finds none).

units.does: didSet of the settings property: updates the lock-backed snapshot, then — unless the load was blocked by file protection — mirrors perf flags, enqueues a disk write and posts flowRecoverySettingsChanged.
units.entry: Swift property observer: runs on every assignment to SettingsManager.settings (all Settings UI bindings, services).

branches.effect: true: log warning and return — change lives only in memory, no save, no notification posted; false: save() + post notification

flags.text: While the load is blocked by file protection every settings mutation (e.g. updateBaseline from a background recording, adoptTrialStart mirror) is kept only in memory and then overwritten when retryLoadAfterUnlock assigns the on-disk settings, so those changes are discarded without a merge.
Observers are not notified while blocked: the guard returns before posting flowRecoverySettingsChanged, so caches (AssistantContextSource) keep stale values for in-memory changes made in that window.

units.does: Nonisolated accessor returning the latest settings value from the lock-backed snapshot box, for off-main readers.

Private nonisolated init: resolves (and migrates) the settings URL, loads it, records the LoadOutcome, seeds settings and the snapshot with the loaded value or UserSettings() defaults, schedules the protected-data observer if blocked, and installs background/terminate flush observers.

log at .info and return the App Group URL; load then reports .fileNotPresent, the app runs on defaults, and the first settings mutation writes those defaults to the App Group path, after which the guard at 115 never migrates again (the legacy file is left in Documents but never read)

flags.text: A failed legacy copy is not retried: the app starts on defaults (.fileNotPresent allows saves), the first settings change creates the App Group file, and from then on the guard skips migration, so the user's Documents settings are permanently abandoned.

units.does: Registers observers for UIApplication.didEnterBackground and willTerminate that synchronously flush any pending settings write.

Static loader: missing file → (nil,.fileNotPresent); successful ISO-8601 JSON decode → (settings,.loaded); NSFileReadNoPermissionError in NSCocoaErrorDomain → (nil,.blockedByProtection); any other read/decode error → (nil,.unreadableOther), logged.

branches.effect: return (nil,.fileNotPresent)
classify the error
true: return (nil,.blockedByProtection); false: log and return (nil,.unreadableOther) — defaults will later be saved over the file

flags.text: Any non-permission failure (including a decode error such as the top-level container being unreadable) yields .unreadableOther, after which the first settings mutation saves defaults over the user's file with no backup copy kept.

units.does: Installs (once) a main-queue observer for protectedDataDidBecomeAvailable that hops to the MainActor and calls retryLoadAfterUnlock.

branches.effect: return; otherwise register one

units.does: Re-runs the static load; stores the new outcome; if settings decoded, assigns them (didSet persists and posts the change notification); then always removes the protected-data observer.

branches.effect: true: replace in-memory settings with them; false: keep in-memory values (now saveable if outcome is fileNotPresent/unreadableOther)
remove it and nil it out

flags.text: The observer is removed unconditionally, even when the retry outcome is still .blockedByProtection; the guard then never lifts for the rest of the process, so every settings change (including Delete All My Data's resetToDefaults) is silently not persisted until relaunch.

units.does: Delete-All-My-Data reset: assigns fresh UserSettings() (didSet persists defaults) and clears the device-local disclaimer flag.

flags.text: If loadOutcome is .blockedByProtection the didSet guard suppresses the save, so the purge resets only memory and the on-disk user_settings.json (age, weight, HR, address) survives the erasure request.

units.does: Writes the three performance flags (enableAIAssistant, enableVoiceMode, enableWatchConnectivity) to standard UserDefaults and enqueues an off-main disk write of the current settings.

flags.text: A failed settings write (disk full, protection) is logged at .info level only (not .warning/.error), so it never appears in Troubleshooting's Recent Problems while the user believes settings were saved.
